qc.label_under_test: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, admiring, criticising, thanking, rewarding or punishing them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in the same way. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us, he feared me); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying, hugging back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.

fire: I always saw her as a mentor, and she in turn saw me as a friend.
We regarded the visiting team as worthy rivals, and they regarded us as the same.
I praised him for his patience, and he praised me for my honesty.
We thanked the volunteers for their hard work, and they thanked us for our support.
I called him a genius, and he laughed and called me a genius too.
We admired the neighbors for their garden, and they admired us for our quiet ways.
I thought of her as family, and it turns out she thought of me as family as well.
I criticised the editor for being too slow, and she criticised me for being too hasty.
quiet: I always saw her as a mentor, and she in turn trusted me.
We regarded the visiting team as worthy rivals, and they visited us the next spring.
I praised him for his patience, and he lent me his car for the weekend.
We thanked the volunteers for their hard work, and they hugged us before leaving.
My boss called me a genius during the meeting yesterday.
We admired the neighbors' garden, and they admired the old oak tree near the fence.
She thought of me as family long before I said anything at all.
The editor criticised me for being hasty, and I criticised her for being too slow.

predictions: Blind test (label-only second author). Expect the label to hold; the 'he laughed and called me' item may run weaker because a verb sits between the clauses.
